headline: Medium risk: MemMachine’s MCP/API outputs can feed PaddleOCR’s document pipeline, creating prompt-injection and data-leakage paths in default integrations.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python interfaces, while PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can run browsers. If MemMachine outputs are routed into PaddleOCR’s document pipeline or browser-driven parsing, attacker-controlled text can be reinterpreted as instructions. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF MemMachine output is copied into PaddleOCR prompts or parsing inputs
IF a shared MCP or browser-mediated channel passes untrusted text between them
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of MemMachine outputs into OCR/parsing prompts
Add a provenance tag and strip instruction-like text before handoff
Use a manual review step before any browser-driven extraction
Restrict the shared channel to read-only artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware filtering between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, and PaddleOCR touches documents and images. If either agent receives the other’s outputs through a shared workspace or API handoff, sensitive content can flow into the other agent’s context and then out through its allowlisted network egress. The shared-data pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF MemMachine context or user facts are placed into documents processed by PaddleOCR
IF PaddleOCR outputs are sent back into MemMachine without redaction
mitigations: Redact personal data before passing artifacts between agents
Keep separate workspaces for conversational memory and documents
Turn off automatic upload of processed outputs
Review allowlisted egress destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-class boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have allowlisted network egress, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git, database, or OAuth scope overlap. The main overlap is network access and API use, which can conflict operationally but does not show a shared mutable resource. Because no stronger write-conflict surface is documented, low is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API resource
IF an orchestrator gives them a shared mutable endpoint without locking
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent
Avoid shared writable endpoints
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Check for duplicate updates in logs
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can emit context-rich outputs, and PaddleOCR is a document-processing system that may consume those outputs as input. If PaddleOCR treats MemMachine’s text as authoritative, OCR or extraction errors can cascade into downstream artifacts. There is no documented verification barrier in either profile, so the interaction is plausible in default integrations and merits medium severity.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR consumes MemMachine-generated text without validation
IF downstream automation acts on OCR output derived from MemMachine context
mitigations: Insert a verification step before downstream use
Require source-document checks for extracted facts
Flag low-confidence OCR results for manual review
Limit automatic actions from parsed text
requires-engineering: add confidence gating and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts and conversational context, while PaddleOCR touches documents and images. The profiles do not show residency, retention, or certification mismatches, so a concrete compliance breach is not established. The only supportable concern is a low-level policy mismatch if the same regulated data class is routed through both systems.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through both agents under different retention rules
IF one agent logs or retains outputs longer than the other
mitigations: Compare retention settings before deployment
Avoid sending regulated data to both agents
Document data-class handling for each agent
Review logs for unexpected persistence
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
